newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/BUND YIELD SPREAD NARROWS POST AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: OLO/BUND YIELD SPREAD NARROWS POST AUCTION.

text.p: Belgian bonds mostly held at their earlier easier levels after Monday's monthly OLO auction, where the Treasury sold a total 28.065 billion francs of March 2007 and March 2001 paper.

"I was surprised by the large amount sold,...surprised that so many people bid so high," said one dealer. "There must have been two big buyers, though the general feeling before the auction was that the market was well offered."
By 1515 GMT the benchmark 2006 OLO yield stood at 6.10 percent versus 6.09 late Friday, its premium over Bunds at eight bp, down from nine earlier and from ll bp at the previous close.
Another dealer said he expected the premium to stay around current levels for now but widen in the longer term. The spread had widened to 11 from eight bp during Friday's session.

One dealer noted a slight steepening of the yield curve. The March 2001 and 2007 OLOs yields were quoted at 4.82 and 6.21 percent respectively, up from average auction yields of 4.796 and 6.196 percent.

Sentiment was expected to remain cautious for the rest of the week, with U.S. consumer confidence, new home sales and GDP data plus the Federal Reserve's beige book due on Wednesday and more U.S. data on Friday when Belgium is closed for a holiday.
Dealers said a strike by workers in the socialist trade union which severely disrupted public transport within the country had little effect on market sentiment.
